summary: This script refreshes a DuckDB database with the latest product catalog by running an API test with Hurl, then loading the validated results into the database. It's designed to run automatically from a cron job, using credentials from a .env file, and will safely skip the database update if the API test fails.

explanations.4: These flags make the script fail fast: -e stops on any error, -u errors on undefined variables, and -o pipefail catches failures in the middle of a pipe chain. This prevents partial updates to the database.
explanations.6: This changes to the directory where the script lives, so all relative paths (like .env and products.hurl) are found correctly no matter where you call the script from.
explanations.10: This loads API_USERNAME and API_PASSWORD variables from the .env file into the current shell session so the next command can use them.
explanations.15: Hurl is an API testing tool that runs the HTTP requests defined in products.hurl; the --test flag makes it validate responses, and if any check fails, it exits with an error (which triggers the set -e from line 4).
explanations.21: Docker runs the DuckDB command-line tool in a container, with --rm cleaning up after, -v mounting the current directory, and -u running as your user so you own the output files.
explanations.25: This feeds the SQL commands from load.sql into DuckDB to insert the validated products.json data into the catalog.duckdb file.
